desc: Fault 205 candidate root cause (see evidence/2026-10-29-gravitylinux-survey.md). 5012 found a secondaries-only write denial over a physical range near the ADT end but read only the legacy CTRR_A/B regs. M4 has a second CTRR instance, CTRR_C (s3_0_c11_c0_0/1, EL1 encodings), enabled on secondaries only; Asahi m1n1 a735ea2+442c7a2+00b8814 and Gravity eb6cab7 reserve it as an FDT mem-rsv, which with idle=nop+arm64.nowfxt makes M4/M4 Pro SMP reliable (Gravity runs all 16 CPUs on M4 Max). Step 1 offline: add the CTRR_C/D/CTXR names from Asahi 442c7a2 to our proxyclient apple_regs.json and t6040-cpu-sysreg-diff.py; cherry-pick a735ea2+00b8814 into the m1n1 fork (keep From: authors). Step 2 rig, reads only: dump CTRR_C/D LWR/UPR/CTL per core and overlay on the 5012 v3 AT bitmap (Asahi says 48 KiB; 5012 saw >256 KiB, explain the gap). Step 3 rig: 217 cow reproducer at maxcpus=2 then 6 with the reservation m1n1; PASS = no 205 fault over the run matrix. Do not drop maxcpus=1 from the daily image until 4000 matrix passes. UPDATE 2026-10-30 (evidence/2026-10-30-t6040-5015-ctrr-macos-abstract-and-live-layout.md): macOS writes no CTRR reg on any CPU, so the window is firmware-locked and a carve-out is the only remedy; macOS reads [3,0,11,1,2/3] with UPR inclusive (last byte UPR+0xfff), so Asahi ALIGN_UP(UPR) is a page short when UPR is aligned. Live boot: m1n1 80badc91 has no CTRR mem-rsv; [adt_end, m1n1 _base) = 384 KiB of allocatable RAM covers 5012s denial. Step 2 now reads [3,0,11,0,0..3], [3,0,11,1,0..5] on the boot CPU AND one secondary, UPR inclusive, overlaid on [adt_end-16K, adt_end+0x60000). Step 3 runs two variants: (a) the Asahi series as-is, (b) a Wallace m1n1 mem-rsv over [adt_end, m1n1 _base); both cmdlines add arm64.nowfxt (CPU has FEAT_WFxT; flokli-code.patch with idle=nop skips WFIT but __delay still loops on WFET). CORRECTION 2026-10-30 (wallace-rex 5495c18): variant (b) reserves the FIXED span [adt_end, adt_end+0x60000), using m1n1 _base only if it equals adt_end+0x60000 (else warn and keep the fixed span), because after a chainload the running stage can sit elsewhere. UPR: if its low 12 bits are zero, the exclusive end = UPR+0x1000 rounded up to 16K and Asahi ALIGN_UP is a page short; if UPR ends in 0xfff, Asahi is right; record which case. Step 3 pass criterion: log any fault OUTSIDE the reserved span (the 2026-07-29 maxcpus=14 boot faulted again about 7.9 MiB above adt_end); one means a second mechanism. The no-IMPDEF/TLBI finding covers the early boot text only.
